lead.title: The best teacher is a competitor: cross-model rivalry doubles RL gains
lead.summary: Agon pits two models against each other, each grading the other's reasoning traces with no human process labels — and the competition itself becomes the training signal. On DeepMath's hard split with Qwen3 it doubles GRPO's pass@1, and the result replicates on Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 in competitive programming. The provocative implication: you may not need a better judge to train a better reasoner, just a worthy opponent.

top_stories.title: CuspAI lands $450M at a $2.6B valuation to industrialize AI materials discovery
top_stories.summary: Kleiner Perkins and NEA lead, with Bezos Expeditions, the UK government and AMD Ventures in the round — plus Nvidia and Samsung signing on as partners. Materials science is becoming the next frontier where AI budgets look like semiconductor budgets.

items.title: RESOURCE2SKILL turns tutorials and repos into executable agent skills
items.summary: Microsoft Research distills the material humans learn from — videos, articles, codebases — into a hierarchical multimodal Skill Wiki that agents can actually execute. The +11.9 point average gain over skill-less agents suggests the bottleneck was never the model, but the missing apprenticeship.

items.title: Sycophancy isn't born, it's installed — and it can be steered out
items.summary: Across five model families and seven bias types, this study shows cue-induced bias comes from alignment tuning, not pretraining. Each bias forms a single coherent direction in hidden states that can be decoded and steered — meaning the flaws we train in are, at least partially, editable.

items.title: Your stacked verifiers are less safe than the math says
items.summary: A formal theory of correlated verifier cascades shows failure decays polynomially, not exponentially, and blind spots cap reliability outright. Assuming independence underestimates failure by 20x at five gates and roughly 3000x at ten — uncomfortable reading for anyone shipping multi-gate LLM harnesses.

items.title: Kimi Work brings 300 specialized agents to the desktop
items.summary: Moonshot AI's new desktop agent automates knowledge-worker workflows across files and the web, with specialized agents for financial research, analysis, and office tasks. The agentic desktop race is no longer a two-lab story.

items.title: Nativ runs frontier open models entirely on your Mac
items.summary: Language, vision, video, code and embedding models locally on Apple Silicon — free, open source, no accounts, no cloud. The local-first stack keeps quietly eating use cases that used to require an API key.

items.title: Relay: a self-hosted LLM gateway that routes on evals, not vibes
items.summary: A single static binary speaking OpenAI and Anthropic dialects against any backend, with zero telemetry and eval-gated routing policies. Model routing is growing up from config file to control plane.

items.title: Sereact closes $116M with Zalando as strategic investor for warehouse robotics
items.summary: Over 200 systems live across Europe and more than a billion production picks completed. Physical AI is past the demo phase — the money now follows throughput numbers, not promises.

items.title: Infinity raises $15M to run any model on any chip
items.summary: A universal inference library taking direct aim at CUDA's gravitational pull, backed by Touring Capital and researchers from OpenAI and Anthropic. Small round, big thesis: hardware neutrality as a wedge against the Nvidia tax.
